## Summary

**CLR** (Clear): Clears destination.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `0 → <ea>` (LineA instruction) |
| Syntax | `CLR <ea>` |
| Short | Clears destination. |
| Description | Clears the destination to zero. Size is byte, word, long or quad. |
| Condition codes | see table |

### Condition codes

| X | N | Z | V | C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| – | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |

### Encoding

Quad:

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–6 | `1010111000` |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |

Others:

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–8 | `01000010` |
| 1 | 7–6 | Size |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |

- Size 0=byte, 1=word, 2= long

### Example

```asm
    clr.q    d0
```

```text
ea d0: (all boxes empty in the original)
Result:
ea d0: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
```

### Notes

- Clr.q is a LineA instruction, set apollo-bit in SR to become active. (ori #$800,sr)
- Do not use, only available on cores 10280 to 10904

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have CLR. This page covers only the 68080 addition: the quad size CLR.Q (LineA encoding). For the classic forms, the Motorola manual applies.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T use CLR.Q: the manual says it is only available on cores 10280 to 10904.
- DO set the Apollo bit (SR bit 11, `ori #$800,sr`) before any LineA instruction.
